chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Hariz, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the sacrifices of the Jews, Christians, and Magians. He said: If you hear them mentioning the Name of God, or a witness for you has seen them mentioning the Name of God, then eat. But if you do not hear them, and no one who saw them testifies to you, then do not eat their sacrifice.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating the meat of Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the permissibility of consuming the meat of the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) and Magians hinges on the explicit invocation of God's Name during slaughter, a condition verified either by direct auditory confirmation or reliable witness testimony. This ruling, found in *al-Istibsar*, reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the actuality of the *tasmiyah* rather than mere presumption, distinguishing it from other schools that may rely on general knowledge of the slaughterer's faith. The inclusion of Magians (Zoroastrians) alongside Jews and Christians highlights the broader application of this rule to monotheistic communities recognized in Islamic law.
